title: Titanium Underwater Camera Housing
alloyReason: Ti-6Al-4V ELI (Grade 23, UNS R56401) is mandated for this deep sea application where ELI elements (O <=0.13%, Fe <=0.25%) provide superior fracture toughness (KIC >100 MPa-m0.5) and fatigue resistance vs standard Grade 5. This rationale is driven by deep-sea camera/sensor pressure housing and fat life requirements.
process: Ring forging radial-axial for deep sea geometry
CNC turn-bore operation for net-shape tolerance
TIG welding autogenous for net-shape tolerance
Hydrostatic pressure test for net-shape tolerance
surfaceTreatment: Heavy-duty passivation 25% HNO3 45min per ASTM B600 for maximum chloride pitting resistance in seawater
commonFailures: HE from over-protection below -0.85V vs Ag/AgCl - controlled by anode current density limiter circuit

faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium Underwater Camera Housing suitable for Deep-sea camera/sensor pressure housing?
faq.a: Titanium Underwater Camera Housing uses Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address deep sea operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium Underwater Camera Housing?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium Underwater Camera Housing require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. deep sea components receive Heavy-duty passivation 25% HNO3 45min per ASTM B600 for maximum chloride pitting resistance in seawater. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the service environment.

faq.q: What quality documentation is included with Titanium Underwater Camera Housing shipments?
faq.a: Each shipment includes: (1) EN 10204 Type 3.1 MTR with full chemical analysis and mechanical properties; (2) Certificate of Conformance; (3) Dimensional inspection report with actual vs nominal measurements; (4) Surface roughness certification on critical features. FAIR available on request.

faq.q: What is the MOQ and typical lead time for Camera housing / Sensor canister deep sea components?
faq.a: Standard MOQ: 1 unit for prototype evaluation. Production lead time: 15-25 business days depending on quantity. Rush orders (3-5 days) available. Contact our supply chain team for volume-based tiered pricing.
